find_organizations.rationale: Returns non-public Sentry account data because it can `Find organizations that the user has access to in Sentry` and `View organizations in Sentry`. No attacker-controlled source or agent-chosen URL/host is advertised.

find_projects.rationale: Returns non-public Sentry data because it can `Find projects in Sentry` and `View projects in a Sentry organization`. It is a SINK because `regionUrl` is a URL used for `self-hosted Sentry installations`, so the tool may contact an agent-chosen host; the advertised text does not state host validation. It is UNTRUSTED under that same least-restrictive reading because an attacker-controlled self-hosted URL could author the returned project data.

update_issue.rationale: Changes Sentry state because it can `Update a Sentry issue's status or assignment`, `resolve, reopen, assign, or ignore an issue`, and `reason` can be `posted as a comment on the issue's activity feed`. It is a SINK because `issueUrl` is a URL and `regionUrl` may identify a `self-hosted Sentry` host; the text does not state host validation. SECRET and UNTRUSTED are kept as undetermined because the output is not described, but the tool operates on non-public Sentry issues and could receive responses from an agent-chosen self-hosted URL.

search_events.rationale: Returns non-public Sentry telemetry because it can `Search Sentry events and replays` across `errors`, `logs`, `spans`, `metrics`, `profiles`, and `replays`. It is UNTRUSTED because those records include attacker-influencable `Application log entries`, exception events, visited pages, replay users, and other production event content. It is a SINK because `regionUrl` can be a URL for `self-hosted Sentry installations`; the text does not state host validation.

analyze_issue_with_seer.rationale: Returns non-public debugging and code information because Seer gives `Root cause analysis`, `Specific file locations and line numbers`, `Concrete code fixes`, and `actual code snippets and fixes` for `production errors`. It is UNTRUSTED because the analysis is based on issue/error details that may include attacker-controlled production error text. It is a SINK because it may `Start new AI analysis` and accepts `issueUrl` plus `regionUrl` for `self-hosted Sentry installations`; the text does not state host validation for those URLs.

search_issues.rationale: Returns non-public Sentry issue data because it can `Search for grouped issues/problems in Sentry` and returns `metadata like title, status, and user count`. It is UNTRUSTED because issue titles and metadata can be derived from attacker-controlled errors, feedback, logs, or event content. It is a SINK because `regionUrl` can be a URL for `self-hosted Sentry installations`; the text does not state host validation.

get_sentry_resource.rationale: Returns non-public Sentry resources because it can `Fetch a Sentry resource` including `issues, events, traces, spans, agent conversations, replays, monitors, preprod snapshots, and snapshot images`. It is UNTRUSTED because events, spans, conversations, replays, and snapshot content may contain attacker-authored application/user content. It is a SINK because it accepts a direct `url` described as a `Sentry URL`; the text does not state that arbitrary hosts are rejected.

search_sentry_tools.rationale: Only searches the `available Sentry MCP tool catalog by name and description` and returns tool names/schemas. The advertised text does not say it fetches user Sentry data, attacker-authored content, executes operations, or contacts an agent-chosen host.

execute_sentry_tool.rationale: Executes dynamic Sentry operations because it can `Execute an available Sentry MCP tool discovered through search_sentry_tools` using arbitrary `arguments`. The catalog may include `project management`, `documentation lookup`, `preprod snapshots`, `attachments`, `DSNs`, `releases`, `teams`, and `issue-specific pivots`, and it can also execute advertised tools that read non-public Sentry data, return attacker-controlled issue/event content, or contact URL/region destinations. It is not HOSTEXEC because the advertised text does not describe arbitrary host code execution.

notes: No advertised flags, environment variables, URL paths, or headers remove tools or labels.
